item.title: Munster In Must-Win Game At Thomond Park
item.description: Munster have a must-win clash with Castres (pr: cast) if they are to guarantee progression to the knock-out stages of the Investec Champions Cup. The Thomond Park fixture gets underway at 5.30. Before that, Leinster go in search of a top-two seeding away to Bayonne (pr: bye-on) from 3.15pm Irish time. item.title: Kerry TD disqualified from driving says there’s no excuse for his actions
item.description: A Kerry TD who was disqualified from driving for two years says there’s no excuse for his actions. Deputy Michael Cahill was convicted of dangerous driving after a court heard he was driving at over 190kph on the M8 motorway last March. He was traveling from Leinster House to a meeting at St. Mary of the Angels in St Francis' Special School in Beaufort when the incident occurred. item.title: Council urged to develop serviced sites schemes across Kerry
item.description: Kerry County Council has been urged to develop serviced sites schemes across Kerry. Fianna Fáil councillor Breandán Fitzgerald raised the motion at a recent Castleisland-Corca Dhuibhne MD meeting. He believes service sites schemes are an affordable option for people, especially in areas where there is not adequate wastewater capacity. item.title: United Victorious Over City In Manchester Derby
item.description: Michael Carrick began his second spell as Manchester United interim head coach with a dominant 2-nil win at home to rivals City in the Premier League. Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu got the goals in the second half of the derby at Old Trafford. Advertisement

item.title: St Brendan's Mauled By Dublin Lions In Cup Final
item.description: Dublin Lions were victorious against St Brendan's Tralee in the Under 18 Men's National Cup Final at the National Basketball Arena in Tallaght. The home side were bigger, stronger and more experienced than the gallant Tralee lads who gave a brave display, particularly in the first two quarter. The Lions were too good in the end taking the title on a 99-54 scoreline. Advertisement

item.title: Cork Defeat Kerry To Win McGrath Cup
item.description: Cork came from behind to beat Kerry 16 points to 15 in the McGrath Cup final at Fitzgerald Stadium. A late point from Chris Og Jones was the difference between the sides after 60 minutes. Advertisement Kerry Manager Jack O'Connor gave his reaction to the result and performance to Tim Moynihan.

item.title: Extension for North Kerry school reaches practical completion
item.description: Significant progress has been made regarding the school capital project for a North Kerry national school. St Brigid’s NS Duagh has reached practical completion on the project, that involves an extension to build four new Special Education Teaching (SET) rooms. Practical completion is the point in a construction project when a building is substantially finished and can be used for its intended purpose. item.title: Permission sought for demolition of stands and other structures at Tralee racecourse
item.description: A Tralee company is seeking permission to demolish all existing buildings at the former Tralee racecourse. Ard Rí Marble has applied to Kerry County Council to demolish structures including the landmark stands, to allow future development of the derelict site. The 100-acre site was sold in 2024 to the Ard-Rí group, owned and run by the Fitzgibbon family, for a price understood to be around €5 million.
